labels.text: List what this account has published, with each page's audience and link.

S33.01.needs: a signed-in AGI account (not Local mode) with at least one published artifact
S33.01.note: Closest match is a plain list, not a dashboard. It shows id, audience and link; no state or per-item actions. The in-chat /artifacts only lists, shows and opens; it has no publish or audience subcommands.
steps: Sign in to an AGI account (not Local mode), then in the terminal type: agi artifacts published
Look at the list: each line shows an artifact id, its audience in brackets, and its link

Compare with Expected: a dashboard of published sites with state and actions. The list shows id, audience and link only, with no state column and no per-site actions; the other actions are separate commands (agi artifacts audience, agi artifacts unpublish)

labels.text: Publish an artifact to a shareable URL.

S33.07.needs: a signed-in AGI account (not Local mode) with a publishable artifact
S33.07.note: The code has no separate preview deployment; publish is the only deploy step and produces the shareable link. Publish refuses artifact kinds the account may not publish.
steps: Sign in to an AGI account (not Local mode), then type: agi artifacts list
Copy an artifact id from the list
Type: agi artifacts publish <id>
Look at the printed result: it should show a share link you can open in a browser, to compare with Expected (a shareable preview URL)

S33.10.needs: a signed-in AGI account (not Local mode) with a publishable artifact; a browser without the AGI sign-in for the last step
S33.10.note: Publish defaults to public (--audience public), so the link is public unless changed.
steps: Sign in to an AGI account (not Local mode) and publish an artifact with: agi artifacts publish <id>
Type: agi artifacts published
Find your artifact in the list and copy its link
Open the link in a browser that is not signed in and check the page loads (compare with Expected: reachable at a public URL)
S33.10.where: agi artifacts publish <id>, then agi artifacts published

labels.text: Change who can open a published artifact: public or workspace.

S33.12.needs: a signed-in AGI account that belongs to a workspace, with a published artifact; a second account in the same workspace and one outside it to test access
S33.12.note: Workspace access is enforced by the server; the CLI only sets the audience. The code also accepts 'organization' and 'org' as aliases.
steps: Sign in to an AGI account (not Local mode) and find a published artifact id with: agi artifacts published
Type: agi artifacts audience <id> workspace
Read the printed result: the audience should now be workspace
Type: agi artifacts published and confirm the entry shows [workspace] (compare with Expected: restricted to workspace members)

labels.text: Take a published artifact's URL away again.

S33.24.needs: a signed-in AGI account with a published artifact; a browser for the last step
S33.24.note: Unpublish removes the share link only; the artifact itself stays in the account. Answering no leaves it published.
steps: Sign in to an AGI account (not Local mode) and find a published artifact id with: agi artifacts published
Type: agi artifacts unpublish <id>, and answer the confirmation prompt with y (or add --yes)
Read the result: it should say the artifact was unpublished and its share link no longer resolves
Open the old share link in a browser and check it no longer loads (compare with Expected: taken offline)

labels.text: Print an artifact's content, or write it to a file.

S33.26.needs: a signed-in AGI account with an artifact that has content; a folder to write into
S33.26.note: No command is named 'source' or 'download'; the closest is show with --out, which writes the artifact's content. Adding --open opens the file in the default app.
steps: Sign in to an AGI account (not Local mode) and find an artifact id with: agi artifacts list
Type: agi artifacts show <id> --out ~/Desktop/test-download (a directory takes the artifact's name; a path without an extension gains one)
Check the printed result shows the written file path
Open the file and check it holds the app's source content (compare with Expected: download the source)

S33.30.needs: a signed-in AGI account with a published artifact, if the tester wants to check unpublish as the nearest step
S33.30.note: No delete command exists for artifacts or apps. The only removal is agi artifacts unpublish <id> (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:1423, apps/cli/src/cloud/artifacts.rs:585), which removes the share link and keeps the artifact. Searched apps/cli/src/lib.rs and apps/cli/src/cloud/artifacts.rs for delete and remove terms, plus the artifacts subcommand enum.
